newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage-backed market lags Treasuries on way up.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage-backed market lags Treasuries on way up.

text.p: Further signs of tame inflation propped mortgage-backed securities prices Thursday, although the upturn trailed behind intermediate Treasuries.
No major economic data were scheduled for Friday, and traders projected range-trade ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee policy meeting.

The Federal Reserve probably will keep interest rates unchanged at least until November, according to economists interviewed by Reuters. Unless mortgage rates resume a downtrend, home refinancing and prepayments were seen stabilizing or ebbing, several participants said.
Although the Mortgage Bankers Association of America said its index would start declining from the 718.8 peak reached in the week ended Aug. 8, some players held prepay protections.

"I would argue that we have a little bit more time" to see strong refinancing activity, as many homeowners are probably in the middle of the process, said one MBS trader. Amid mixed market prepay sentiment, he added, "we try to keep our bigger positions hedged as well as we can."
Most mortgage-backed securities (MBS) were up as much as 3/8 late Thursday, with the largest gains in the discount coupons that usually are used as shelter from prepayments.
The MBS gains across the board, however, were overshadowed by the 18/32 rise in 10-year Treasury notes.

At 6.27 percent, the 10-year note yield was still above the recent 6.00 percent low that analysts said was a catalyst for swift prepayments. Yet the yield slid quickly from a closing level of 6.40 percent just two days ago, as concerns about an imminent Fed rate hike faded.

The MBS trader contended that refinancings would persist at a strong pace for another month, in a lagged response to recent rate lows. "By that time, we could have rates down again," generating another refinancing wave, he added.
The latest fuel for lower Treasury yields was a 0.2 percent rise in July consumer prices, which was in line with forecasts. July industrial production and capacity utilization were also moderate.

Among 30-year 7 1/2-percent MBS, Government National Mortgage Association bonds rose 11/32 to 101-10/32 to yield 7.33 percent, Freddie Macs gained 9/32 to 101-15/32 for a yield of 7.28 percent and Fannie Maes advanced 9/32 to 101-10/32 to yield 7.27 percent.
Premium bonds edged up by 2/32 to 9/32, while discount bonds were mostly 8/32 to 13/32 higher on the day.
